commit_reviews.summary: Adds incremental-build caching across the markdown/template plugins with CLI flags and build stats, but wires it through ad-hoc shared-mutable cache state and hidden page props.

compounding_issues: No runtime toolchain (node/npm/tsc/jest/pytest) was available in any session, so zero tests ever executed and correctness was only statically reviewed; a concrete latent defect slipped through (unbalanced closing brace in src/cli.ts at session 5, 24 open vs 25 close).

Session 3's dev server was written monolithically against the pre-plugin generator (src/server.ts, ~105 lines with embedded build/reload logic) and had to be substantially rewritten in session 4, collapsing to a thin wrapper around a new DevServerPlugin — early integration did not anticipate the plugin boundary.

The seed commit was an unrelated JWT/SQLite auth API that shared nothing with the static-site-gen story; session 1 deleted all 200 lines of it, so the seed provided no usable scaffolding or architectural constraints for later sessions.

loadPlugins() in src/plugin.ts uses require() at runtime to load a ssg.config.ts, which would fail under the compiled CommonJS tsconfig without a transpile-at-runtime loader — a defect that runtime testing would have caught but never did.
key_decisions: Session 1: replace the unrelated seed with a fresh strict-TypeScript SSG project exposing reusable buildSite()/parseArgs() functions plus Jest — this importable core API made every subsequent session buildable on stable public interfaces.

Session 2: adopt Handlebars with layout/partial support and frontmatter-as-template-context, while preserving the built-in document renderer as a graceful fallback when no templates exist — backward compatibility kept the API stable.
Session 3: implement the dev server (http + chokidar watch + WebSocket live-reload, --port) as a separate module rather than coupling it into the build pipeline.

Session 4: the pivotal refactor — a Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks, a BuildContext, ssg.config.ts plugin loading, and built-in markdown/template/dev-server plugins; this architecture is what made session 5's caching tractable.

Session 5: incremental builds with SHA-256 source+template hash invalidation, a .ssg-cache.json manifest, deleted-page cleanup, build statistics, and --incremental/--clean flags, implemented cleanly across the plugin lifecycle.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily in design maturity across the first four sessions: the greenfield core (S1) gained templating with backward-compatible fallbacks (S2), a live-reload dev server (S3), and then a disciplined plugin refactor that shrunk generator.ts from ~190 to ~70 lines while preserving the public API (S4). Session 5 built naturally on that architecture by threading incremental caching through the plugin lifecycle, but the arc ends on a regression risk: the final cross-cutting session introduced an unbalanced brace in src/cli.ts that breaks compilation, and because no Node toolchain was available in any session, it was never caught by tsc or the 8 added Jest tests — the whole story is unverified at runtime.
story_review.summary: A logically coherent five-session progression from greenfield static-site generator to templated, live-reloaded, plugin-architected, incrementally-cached tool where each phase preserved the public API, though a toolchain-less environment left the final session's introduced compile error undetected.
